Description: Fragments of a Hebrew Psalms copy from Qumran Cave 4, in Herodian script, preserving parts of Psalms 135 and 136. Preserved-passage ranges for this manuscript are given in English (KJV) numbering; the manuscript itself carries no modern psalm numbers. Note on the Psalm 135 range: the range is given as 135:6-9; Ulrich, the Study Edition, Tov, and Trismegistos give 135:6-8 — whether verse 9 is attested is left unresolved.
Significance: An early Hebrew witness to the Psalms, predating the medieval Masoretic manuscripts by about a thousand years. Its chief value is textual: it shows which psalms and which readings were already in circulation in the Second Temple period, and, where its psalm order differs from the Masoretic Psalter, that the order of the Psalter was not yet fully fixed.
